extraction_scope: Worker-6 final mechanism adjudication from primary XML/PDF locators. Direct mechanism claims are limited to assays directly performed in this paper; proposed model is kept as model-level synthesis.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: (KW)4 directly localizes to bacterial cell surfaces in the tested E. coli and S. aureus strains.
The KW-repeat peptides bind LPS with chain-length-dependent displacement of dansyl polymyxin B, with longer peptides also showing LPS-associated conformational changes.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=29:Interaction of peptides with LPS; xml:fig=4

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Active KW-repeat peptides disrupt bacterial cytoplasmic membranes, supported by membrane depolarization and SYTOX Green uptake assays in E. coli and S. aureus.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=30:Membrane lytic and bactericidal activities of the peptides; xml:fig=5

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Model-membrane assays support bilayer permeabilization and lipid interaction, especially for (KW)4 and (KW)5, without converting the schematic model into a directly visualized pore mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: (KW)4 causes bacterial surface damage/clumping and agglutination in source-described SEM and agglutination experiments; this is kept as phenotype-level support for membrane disruption/agglutination.
